title: Adaptive Console Layout & Cross-Browser Resilience for Tables, Charts, and Modals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal:
Deliver an adaptive layout system and visual refinements for the Redwood Console pages (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) to ensure consistent behavior across modern browsers and common device sizes. Scope focuses on: tables (large result sets and column behavior), charts (SVG/canvas rendering and resizing), and modals (stacking, focus management, and mobile presentation).

Background:
Several teams have reported subtle regressions when the Console is used in Safari/iPad and older Chromium builds: clipped table columns, chart rerender flicker on resize, and modals that lose focus or have buggy scroll locking. This ticket consolidates design decisions, creates prototypes for engineering to implement, and captures cross-browser test cases.

Design decisions and rationale:
- Layout: adopt a hybrid grid/flex approach: CSS grid for coarse page regions (header, primary column, secondary column) and flexbox for intra-panel content. This gives predictable reflow at breakpoints while avoiding IE-only grid quirks.
- Tables: show a condensed row variant at <= 900px, enable column horizontal scroll for deep tables, and implement sticky headers using transform-based techniques to avoid repaint storms in Safari. We recommend virtualization (ENG owns) for >10k rows; design provides the collapsed/expanded row states and empty-state treatments.
- Charts: default to SVG for small charts for accessibility (ARIA) and switch to canvas render paths for very high-series charts. Provide a resize debounce and placeholder skeleton to avoid layout shifts during container changes.
- Modals: mobile-first modal sheet pattern for <=560px, centered dialog for larger screens. Ensure focus trap and keyboard navigation, and prefer z-index token system to avoid stacking context bugs. For browsers with inconsistent overflow behavior (iOS Safari), use a body locking shim managed by the runtime.
- Cross-browser fallbacks: avoid relying on experimental CSS (e.g., container queries) unless polyfilled; when using CSS variables for theme tokens, provide a JS fallback for older browsers.
- Accessibility: ensure 44px minimum touch targets, semantic table markup, and descriptive chart labels for screen readers.

Prototype highlights:
- Figma frames cover three breakpoints: desktop (1280+), tablet (768–1279), and mobile (<768). Each frame includes example dashboard with a heavy table and two chart widgets, plus a modal flow for editing routes.
- Clickable prototype demonstrates: sticky header behavior with long tables, chart resize when toggling sidepanel, and bottom sheet modal on mobile.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Performance vs fidelity: canvas path increases perf but reduces DOM-accessible semantics; we'll keep SVG for primary dashboards and switch to canvas when telemetry indicates rendering bottlenecks.
- Full container queries would simplify breakpoint logic but require a polyfill for stable cross-browser support; engineering prefers to defer until broad support or an established polyfill is available.
- Table virtualization is engineering-heavy; design will supply states/animations but rely on ENG-2874 for implementation.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Visual parity across latest Chrome, Firefox, Safari (macOS), Edge (Windows) and iOS Safari (iPad).
2) Tables: sticky headers work without repaint flicker; collapsed/condensed rows available at defined breakpoint.
3) Charts: no layout shift on panel toggles; legends remain accessible.
4) Modals: focus trap and scroll lock behave consistently on desktop and mobile.
5) QA checklist added to Confluence with explicit browser/device repros.

Next steps / action items:
- Design: finalize Figma frames and deliver redlines for engineering (owner: Jonas) — due 2025-01-20.
- Research: quick A/B with 6 internal users on iPad and older Chromium to validate touch targets and modal sheet (owner: Aisha) — test window 2025-01-22 to 2025-01-29.
- Engineering: provide implementation feasibility feedback on sticky header approach and chart render strategies (owner: ENG-2874) — expected 2025-01-24.
- PM: triage prioritization for release candidate and coordinate QA windows (owner: Maria Gomez).

Notes:

- Logged cross-browser issues to reproduce during QA: Safari column clip (ref: case 001), chart jitter on resize (case 002), modal scroll lock failure on iOS (case 003).
